substeps.label: 1/4 The bottle trip
substeps.caption: Liquid waste leaves a station only in the capped bottle it was made in. One class a trip: this unit carries a 1 L bottle of sieve-wash IPA, its fines kept wet, in the spill tray on its deck.

substeps.label: 1/4 The bottle trip
substeps.caption: It drives to the ducted fume hood's dock. Never the IPA and the Weck's together, never the acid and the sulfide, never anything aqueous with powder waste: the unit's job list knows each bottle's class.

substeps.label: 2/4 The cabinets
substeps.caption: The hood's base is two vented cabinets. A person moves each day's bottles into them, checks labels and dates, and files the pickup request.

substeps.label: 2/4 The cabinets
substeps.caption: Solvent cabinet: the sieve-wash IPA with its Al fines in a grounded can, the rinse IPA, the Form Wash IPA with resin and the used BN cans. Acid cabinet: Acid Aqueous and Weck's a shelf apart, each in its own tray.

substeps.label: 2/4 The cabinets

substeps.label: 3/4 The powder point
substeps.caption: Powder waste stays where it is made: the powder point stands in the atomizer's area, behind the rePowder's fire point, with a vacuum, a pail and a lid for each alloy family.

substeps.label: 3/4 The powder point
substeps.caption: Each family has its own 118EXP and its own grounded steel pail: Al and Cu residues never share a bin (aluminium with copper oxide is a thermite pair).

substeps.label: 3/4 The powder point
substeps.caption: Loose powder and sweepings go in the Solid Material bucket, used filters straight into dry sand. When a pail is full, the pickup is requested from BYU Risk Management.

substeps.label: 3/4 The vacuum liners
substeps.caption: A person changes the liners; the arms don't. In from the aisle round the glovebox and along the corridor behind the machines, clear of the fire point, to the Al-family 118EXP.

substeps.label: 3/4 The vacuum liners
substeps.caption: Vacuum off and unplugged, after its run-on and 60 s settle (vacuum SOP 4). The two clamps open and the head comes off (set aside: not drawn).

substeps.label: 3/4 The vacuum liners
substeps.caption: Vacuum off and unplugged, after its run-on and 60 s settle (vacuum SOP 4). The two clamps open and the head comes off (set aside: not drawn).

substeps.label: 3/4 The vacuum liners
substeps.caption: The liner is sealed where it is: its mouth drawn up, twisted into a gooseneck, folded over and taped (vacuum SOP 4.4). Dry: no water, no oil, nothing poured.

substeps.label: 3/4 The vacuum liners

substeps.label: 3/4 The vacuum liners
substeps.caption: The sealed liner comes out by its neck, over the vacuum's handle, to the Al-family pail beside it on the corridor side.

substeps.caption: A fresh liner, seated on bare metal, the head back on and clamped, plugged in. Powder waste never rides a MiR: the full pail waits here for BYU Risk Management's pickup.

substeps.label: 3/4 The vacuum liners
substeps.caption: And out the way they came. The liners, the bottles and the labels are booked in upkeep as the waste work: an hour a week at one alloy a day.

substeps.label: 4/4 Where waste waits
substeps.caption: Two places on the floor: powder at the powder point by the atomizer, liquids under the fume hood across the aisle. Waste stays in the room it was made in, incompatible classes apart.
